title: GIFT-Eval-CTX: A Benchmark For Contextual Forecasting Model Evaluation

claim.summary: GIFT-Eval-CTX builds 10,000 hard GIFT-Eval test windows annotated with structured Macro and Micro future effects through validator-gated discovery agents and a blind-first critic, and measures how well forecasters convert that verified context into numerical trajectories.

tasks.source_label: Forecasting and prediction; time series annotation

modules.name: Validator-gated structured temporal effect annotation
modules.scope_reason: Agents propose trend, seasonality and interval-bounded excursion, mean-shift or seasonal-change effects that deterministic validators recompute from the raw series; the schema and checks describe any series segment and would survive a change of task family, although the residual overview tool here uses TSFM forecasts.
evidence_locators: PDF p.4; passage beginning "the pipeline first runs independent"
PDF p.3; passage beginning "Free-form descriptions confound the information"

modules.name: Blind-first joint critic review
modules.scope_reason: Forming an independent reading before viewing other agents' proposals, then supporting, revising or excluding them, is a domain-independent multi-agent review order.
evidence_locators: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Blind-first Joint Critic Agent. After"

modules.name: Paired history-only and structured-context forecasting evaluation
modules.scope_reason: Each instance pairs a history with a future target and effects, and scoring compares the same forecaster's MASE with and without the effects, so the resource is bound to the forecasting output.
evidence_locators: PDF p.3; passage beginning "GIFT-Eval-CTX supports a paired evaluation"
